verdict.rationale: Vue's official docs list a first-party "Migration from Vue 2" guide, so an official upgrade path exists for the major version jump. The release policy adds that deprecated features keep working until the next major release, and TypeScript users should upgrade manually when a new minor ships. The guide appears only as a navigation title, though, so its depth and step-by-step content are unproven. Missing for 10: evidence of the guide's actual content (breaking-change lists, migration build or codemods, step-by-step instructions), upgrade guidance for minor versions, and hands-on corroboration that developers followed it successfully.

support.subject: As a developer, I can follow an official upgrade guide to move my existing project to a newer version

citations.quote: Deprecated features will continue to work, and will be removed in the next major release after it entered deprecated status.
If you are using TypeScript, you can use a semver range that locks the current minor and manually upgrade when a new minor version of Vue is released.
